title: AI and Machine Learning in Transaction Monitoring
summary: How firms move from rules-based to AI-driven monitoring using anomaly detection and network analytics, and the detection trade-offs supervisors should expect firms to manage.
topic: Reducing Financial Crime & Delivering Market Integrity
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How firms move from rules-based to AI-driven monitoring using anomaly detection and network analytics, and the detection trade-offs supervisors should expect firms to manage.
Learning Objectives: Explain how AI and machine learning techniques are applied to transaction monitoring
Assess claims about false-positive reduction and detection performance
Challenge whether systems are tuned for detection rather than workload
Syllabus: Rules-based versus AI-driven monitoring: capabilities and limits
Anomaly detection, behavioural profiling and graph analytics
False positives, false negatives and reading performance metrics critically
Case study: an AI monitoring system under supervisory review
Intended Audience: AML/CFT, sanctions and financial crime supervisors and inspectors
Market surveillance, conduct and data analytics staff working on financial crime risk
Senior managers shaping the authority's financial crime strategy and use of SupTech
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of AML/CFT, sanctions or conduct supervision is helpful. No technical background in AI or data science is required.
Core Reading: FATF, International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations (as updated)
FATF, Opportunities and Challenges of New Technologies for AML/CFT (2021)
